newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian sorghum market steady - Grainco.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian sorghum market steady - Grainco.

text.p: Australia's new crop sorghum market remains relatively steady with limited tonnage traded and growers not selling, Queensland grain cooperative Grainco Ltd's trading manager Rob Brealey said in the weekly market report.
Domestic bids rose marginally last week on slight strength in the futures market, he said.
This was against the background of the USDA November corn production report which surprised the market by increasing the U.S. crop estimate to just over 9.2 billion bushels.
This was above expectations and continued the bearish tone of the market, he said.
While the report was bearish for the market longer-term, in the short-term there had been some support from strength in the soybean and wheat markets, he said.
The lower corn price in the U.S. has resulted in many growers in Australia becoming reluctant sellers at present, giving the market some support.
Longer-term, increasing world feed grain stocks continue to weigh on the market.
Australia's domestic feed barley market firmed last week on a combination of unfavourable harvest weather, reluctant grower selling and a tight freight market, he said.
"With the wheat market also a little firmer over the past week, the short-term tone appears to have changed somewhat," Brealey said.
Internationally, the feed barley market remains steady to a little lower. The European Union subsidy issue remains an important element for markets to watch.
International export levels for malt barley appear supported in the short-term as international buyers attempt to gauge Australia's malting barley harvest.

Overseas demand for Australian malting barley remains steady to a little lower with a stabilising effect on the local market. As the Australian harvest progresses, the export price differential between feed and malt barley values needs to be closely watched for future pricing trends, he said.
Domestically, values were steady over the past weeek.
Cool weather over the past few weeks has seen the cotton crop stagnate in many areas. A return to more seasonal temperatures should put on a spurt of growth for the crop, he said.
Overall production is unlikely to be affected and a record crop seems to be well on line, he said.
The market has been relatively flat with domestic interest still thin and export consumers in inquiry mode.

Consumers in the Indian sub-continent continue to put pressure on Australia's chickpea market. While they require Australian product, aggressive pricing from Australian exporters is keeping a lid on the market, he said.
Reports of some damage in the southern Australian crop have been largely disregarded by the export market.
Domestic oilseeds values were firmer over the past week.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
